messages:
alex.finops: Heads-up — saw a ~3.6x spike in nightly GPU hours for EU on the Burncard routes between 02:00-04:00 UTC. Dashboard (finops/burncard/nightly) shows model 'burncard-v2' dominating, but cloud invoice doesn't match by ~12%. Can someone sanity-check?

maria.eng: ugh ok — is this the per-model breakdown or per-route?

alex.finops: per-model breakdown. The route-level view (routes/burncard) shows steady request count, so looks like longer seq lengths or runaway concurrency.

sam.ops: I can tail the autoscaler logs for that window. suspiciously similar to last month's midnight maintenance window. Starting logs now.

lee.data: pulling raw billing export + model telemetry. quick SQL to join tokens vs billed GPU hours: 
```sql
SELECT day, model, SUM(token_count) as tokens, SUM(gpu_seconds) as gpu_s FROM model_usage
WHERE day='2024-09-18' AND region='eu' AND model LIKE 'burncard%'
GROUP BY day, model;
```
I'll post results in a sec.

infra-bot: deploy-monitor: autoscaler scaled pool eu-gpu-prod from 24 -> 92 nodes at 02:03 UTC due to surge in pending queue.

lee.data: result: burncard-v2 tokens up 2.1x, gpu_seconds up 3.8x. Average sequence length jumped ~1.8x. But the billed GPU hours from cloud CSV is +4.3x. mismatch ~12% as alex noted.

maria.eng: could be preemptible node churn — ephemeral GPU reclaim leads to lower efficiency and double-counted VM-hours in cloud report? also check if we failed to tag some nodes so they get attributed to a different project/billing tag.

sam.ops: checked node tags — all eu-gpu-prod had correct billing tags. However there's a pattern: a transient networking issue at 02:07 caused 14 nodes to re-register. Re-registration caused instance uptime to restart, which might show as extra VM-hours on the cloud side. Logs attached: `autoscaler.log` lines 1184-1210 show re-register events.

alex.finops: ok, so action items: 1) infra to confirm node churn -> sam, 2) data to reconcile token->gpu delta and generate per-route effective cost -> lee, 3) ops to check cloud-hour attribution / API for reclaimed instances -> maria.

lee.data: I'll produce a short dashboard delta widget: per-model tokens, gpu_seconds, cloud_vm_hours, and ratio. Will add a test alert if ratio > 1.2 for future nights.

maria.eng: also recommend adding a billing tag audit to nightly runbook and a cheap synthetic load test to exercise the long-tail seq lengths — if prompt engineering changed, we need to cap max seq or enable prefix caching.

sam.ops: confirmed node churn correlates with a router flap in europe-2 at 02:06 UTC. Networking team ticket created: NET-4381. Will include timeline and node IDs.

alex.finops: thanks — please drop the reconciled numbers in this thread when ready. If cloud overcount is due to re-registration we can file a credit claim but we should also add a guard in the autoscaler to avoid transient reboots causing billable restarts. :memo: :chart_with_upwards_trend:

infra-bot: ticket NET-4381 created by sam.ops. Related: incident doc linked: https://redwood.internal/incidents/NET-4381

lee.data: attaching reconciled numbers (summary): tokens -> gpu_seconds ratio consistent; cloud_vm_hours higher by 11.9% attributable to 14 re-registrations. Proposed short-term fix: treat <5min re-register as continuation for billing attribution and add alerting.

maria.eng: sounds good. I'll schedule a follow-up next week to model financial impact if this repeats across regions (quick sim suggests ~0.6% monthly burn if it recurs weekly).

alex.finops: great — closing loop when NET-4381 has postmortem. Thanks all.
